audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer builds the entire lane around 'track Scrap Shield', and phases[0]/breakdown.early tell the player 'your passive shield already blanks his chip'.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is a 6-second shield-and-speed button; tracking a 6s cooldown is not a lane plan, and it does not stop dashes, so 'E-punch into his Scrap Shield (it catches you mid-dash)' is simply false. Galio has no passive shield either — Colossal Smash is 'Galio's next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area', pure offence. The mirror audit at audits/top/rumble__galio.json flagged the same phantom passive shield from Rumble's side.
audit.corrected: The lane is decided by the Heat bar and Flamespitter (10/9/8/7/6s), not Scrap Shield. Colossal Smash is an empowered auto, not a shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is marked Skill while whys[4] calls Hero's Entrance 'your hard spike', and the whole page says the lane is Galio's from 3 onward.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s with 4000-5500 range and lands on an ally's position — the mirror states the consequence exactly: alone in the side lane it is no threat to Rumble, but it wins any fight where an ally is standing. That is a Galio row, not a Skill row.
audit.corrected: Level 6 flipped to Galio in both layers. Levels 2, 3, First item and Two+ items also read Galio in the prose, but 'Rumble' (6 chars) cannot become 'Galio' (5) inside the +/-10% band — flagged.
sources: existing content whys[1], whys[2], whys[4], whys[5]

audit.whatIsWrong: Two interactions absent, one asserted falsely. Missing: Electro Harpoon reduces magic resist, and Overheating locks Rumble out of casting entirely. Falsely asserted: Scrap Shield catching Galio mid-dash.
audit.why: Riot on Electro Harpoon: 'slowing their Move Speed, and reducing their Magic Resist', 850 range, two charges. That directly attacks the stat this page tells you to stack and the reason it claims your W blanks him. Riot on Junkyard Titan: 'When he reaches 100% Heat, he starts Overheating, gaining bonus Attack Speed and granting his basic attacks bonus damage, but making him unable to cast spells for a few seconds.' That is the taunt window — no Scrap Shield, no harpoon, no Flamespitter. Riot on Scrap Shield: 'Rumble pulls up a shield, protecting him from damage and granting him a quick burst of speed' — no dash-stopping anywhere in it.
audit.corrected: Harpoon shreds your MR from 850 with two charges; commit at 100 Heat when he cannot cast; Scrap Shield is a 6s shield that does nothing to your dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Scrap Shield as matchup-defining and carries no numbers.
audit.why: Flamespitter 10/9/8/7/6s is the cooldown that decides trades; Scrap Shield's 6s makes it uncountable. The Equalizer is 130/105/80s. Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7s.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block rewritten around Flamespitter, Heat and the Equalizer.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid says 'Punish the instant he dumps Overheat — Flamespitter is on a long cooldown after'.
audit.why: Flamespitter is 10s at rank 1, not long, and Overheat is not something he dumps — it is a state he enters at 100 Heat during which he cannot cast at all while gaining attack speed and bonus auto damage. Punishing it means taunting him inside the no-cast window, not chasing a long cooldown that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Overheat reframed as the cast lockout it actually is.

edits.before: Level 1 belongs to Rumble: Flamespitter out-DPSes your one empowered Colossal Smash auto, so don't contest it — sidestep the cone and last-hit from max range. The lane flips at 3 once you have Q-W-E. His damage is almost entirely magic, which is exactly what Shield of Durand is built to soak: bait him into burning Flamespitter, channel W as the flame ticks to ramp your magic-amplified damage reduction, then release the taunt and chain Justice Punch's dash-knockup. Respect Electro Harpoon — the slow is how he kites you out of your fixed-distance E.
edits.after: Level 1 belongs to Rumble: Flamespitter out-DPSes your one Colossal Smash auto, so don't contest it — sidestep the 600 cone and last-hit at range. The lane flips at 2, when Winds of War pokes from 825 and outranges the cone entirely. His damage is almost all magic, exactly what Shield of Durand soaks: bait Flamespitter, charge W as the flame ticks, then release the taunt into Justice Punch. But respect Electro Harpoon — 850 range, and it shreds your magic resist as well as slowing you, so it chips away at the stat this whole plan rests on.

edits.before: This is your window. From 4 to 6 his only trade is sitting in Flamespitter, and Shield of Durand turns that magic damage into a near-nullified channel while the release-taunt locks him for your E. At 6, Hero's Entrance is the swing: channel the shield through an Equalizer commit and land the all-in, or rotate out and cash R for a kill mid or bot while top stays even. Punish the instant he dumps Overheat — Flamespitter is on a long cooldown after and he's left without his main damage source.
edits.after: This is your window. From 4 to 6 his only real trade is parking you in Flamespitter (10s at rank 1), and Shield of Durand turns that magic damage into a near-nullified charge while the release-taunt locks him for your E. At 6, Hero's Entrance is the swing: charge the W through an Equalizer commit and land the all-in, or rotate out and cash R elsewhere. The cleanest punish is Overheat — at 100 Heat he cannot cast at all for a few seconds, and that is when you taunt him.

edits.before: You don't fall off versus Rumble the way you would into a true hypercarry — he's a teamfight zone-control bruiser, not a hard scaler, and your anti-AP profile keeps soaking his magic. His one real threat is a perfectly placed Equalizer over a chokepoint in a 5v5, so respect the ult line and keep your team from clumping in it. Your value is the map: use Hero's Entrance to engage from fog, taunt his backline off your carries, and turn every Flamespitter commit into a free pick. Close the game around objectives where your global presence beats his single-lane footprint.
edits.after: You don't fall off versus Rumble the way you would into a true hypercarry — he's a teamfight zone-control bruiser, not a hard scaler, and your anti-AP profile keeps soaking his magic. Two caveats: Electro Harpoon shreds magic resist, so his poke improves the more of it you stack, and a well-placed Equalizer over a chokepoint in a 5v5 is still a fight-winner. Your value is the map: use Hero's Entrance to engage from fog, taunt his backline off your carries, and turn every Flamespitter commit into a free pick. Close around objectives where your global beats his single-lane footprint.

notes: Mirror reconciled against audits/top/rumble__galio.json: both sides now say Rumble owns Level 1 and Galio owns Level 2 onward, both use Justice Punch 650 / 11-to-7s, Shield of Durand 275 taunt / 18-to-14s, Hero's Entrance 180s landing on an ALLY, and both call out that Galio has no passive shield. I did not repeat their harpoon-the-W-charge line from this side because it is their play, not the Galio player's. Rumble's Scrap Shield carries derived 'knockup' and 'terrain' flags in the kit library that Riot's description ('pulls up a shield, protecting him from damage and granting him a quick burst of speed') does not support — those bogus flags produced a 'Both sides carry displacement (Scrap Shield (W) vs Hero's Entrance (R))' row in _missing-interactions.json which I ignored, and they are almost certainly the origin of the false 'Scrap Shield catches you mid-dash' line on the live page. Galio's Justice Punch has the same problem with a bogus 'terrain' flag. content.win[1], win[2], win[5], win[6] and the matching phases sides still read 'Rumble' while every why on those rows describes Galio winning; 'Rumble' (6) to 'Galio' (5) is outside the length band so I could not fix them.
